extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers, pass-through entities, material advisors, tax professionals, and legal counsel involved in syndicated conservation easement transactions
extracted.subtask_description: Final Treasury/IRS regulations identifying certain syndicated conservation easement transactions (and substantially similar transactions) as listed transactions for purposes of §1.6011-4, imposing disclosure obligations on participants and material advisors and setting bright-line and definitional rules (including a 2.5× test and methods to calculate investor investment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements identifying a syndicated conservation easement as a listed transaction (paragraph (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A transaction is identified as a listed transaction if it meets the elements in paragraph (b): promotional materials offer the possibility of allocating to the taxpayer a charitable contribution deduction that equals or exceeds 2.5 times the taxpayer's investment in the pass-through entity; the pass-through entity donates a real property interest (e.g., conservation easement) within three years following the taxpayer's investment; the pass-through entity allocates a charitable contribution deduction to the taxpayer and the taxpayer claims that deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements, taken together, identify the listed transaction. The regulations provide examples and a rebuttable presumption in certain circumstances. Transactions that substitute fee simple or other real property interests, or are substantially similar, may also be treated as the same listed transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Charitable contribution deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'charitable contribution deduction' means a deduction under section 170 of the Internal Revenue Code, which includes a deduction arising from a qualified conservation contribution as defined in section 170(h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Conservation easement
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'conservation easement' means a restriction (granted in perpetuity) on the use which may be made of the real property, within the meaning of section 170(h)(2)(C) of the Code, exclusively for conservation purposes as defined in section 170(h)(1)(C) and (h)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Pass-through entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'pass-through entity' means a partnership, S corporation, or trust (other than a grantor trust within the meaning of subchapter J of chapter 1 of the Code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Promotional materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional materials includes materials described in §301.6112-1(b)(3)(iii)(B) and any other written or oral communication regarding the transaction provided to investors, such as marketing materials, appraisals (preliminary, draft, and the appraisal attached to the return), websites, transactional documents (deeds of conveyance), private placement memoranda, tax opinions, operating agreements, subscription agreements, statements of anticipated value of the conservation easement, and statements of the anticipated amount of the charitable contribution deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple promotional materials differ, the highest suggested or implied charitable contribution deduction amount governs whether the 2.5× rule is met. Whether all promotional materials, taken as a whole, make an offer is a factual determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Qualified organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'qualified organization' means an organization described in section 170(h)(3) of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Real property
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'real property' includes all land, structures, and buildings, including a certified historic structure as defined in section 170(h)(4)(C) of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Substantially similar
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'substantially similar' is defined in §1.6011-4(c)(4). For example, transactions that meet the elements of paragraph (b) except that the pass-through entity contributes a fee simple interest in real property or a real property interest described in section 170(h)(2)(A) or (B) rather than a conservation easement are substantially similar to the listed transaction identified in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations treat fee-simple or other real-property-interest substitutions as substantially similar; thus such transactions fall within the listing if they meet the other elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2.5 times rule — bright-line (paragraph (d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions for which the promotional materials offer the taxpayer the possibility of being allocated a charitable contribution deduction of only an amount less than 2.5 times the taxpayer's investment and for which the taxpayer is actually allocated a charitable contribution deduction of an amount less than 2.5 times the taxpayer's investment are generally not considered substantially similar to the listed transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if a pass-through entity engages in a series of transactions with a principal purpose of avoiding this bright-line rule, the series may be disregarded or the arrangement recharacterized based on all facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple suggested contribution amounts (paragraph (d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If promotional materials suggest or imply a range of possible charitable contribution deduction amounts, the highest suggested or implied amount determines whether the 2.5 times rule is met. If one promotional material states a higher amount than others, the highest stated amount controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttable presumption of meeting the 2.5 times rule (paragraph (d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2.5 times rule is deemed met (rebuttable presumption) if: the pass-through entity donates a real property interest within three years following the taxpayer's investment; the pass-through entity allocates a charitable contribution deduction to the taxpayer equal to or exceeding 2.5 times the taxpayer's investment; and the taxpayer claims a charitable contribution deduction equal to or exceeding 2.5 times the taxpayer's investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption may be rebutted if the taxpayer establishes to the Commissioner's satisfaction that none of the promotional materials contained a suggestion or implication that investors might be allocated a deduction equal to or exceeding 2.5 times their investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods to determine taxpayer's investment (paragraph (d)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A taxpayer may determine the amount of their investment in the pass-through entity using either the anti-stuffing method or, for contributions made after December 29, 2022, the relevant basis method. No other methods may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-stuffing method (paragraph (d)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the anti-stuffing method, the amount of a taxpayer's investment is the portion of the cash or fair market value of assets the taxpayer used to acquire its interest in the pass-through entity that is attributable to the real property on which a conservation easement is placed (or the portion thereof) that gives rise to the charitable contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts attributable to other property held by the pass-through entity (cash, securities, other assets) are excluded. Assets retained to pay operation and maintenance costs are not attributable to the real property and thus excluded. The rules also apply with appropriate adjustments when the transaction involves a substantially similar transaction where a fee simple is donated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant basis method (paragraph (d)(4)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For contributions made after December 29, 2022, taxpayers may use their relevant basis, as determined under section 170(h)(7)(B) of the Code and §1.170A-14(k), as the amount of their investment for purposes of the 2.5 times rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples and factual assumptions (paragraph (d)(5) examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation includes examples (e.g., Example 1 and Example 2) that illustrate application of the anti-stuffing method, the calculation of attributable portions of acquisition cost, how promotional materials' stated allocations are evaluated, and how fee simple contributions are treated as substantially similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples assume partnerships are respected for Federal tax purposes and allocations comply with subchapter K; they show step-by-step calculations of investment attributable to donated property for applying the 2.5× test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of participation (paragraph (e)(1)–(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a taxpayer has participated in a syndicated conservation easement transaction is determined under §1.6011-4(c)(3)(i)(A). Participants include: an owner of a pass-through entity; a pass-through entity; and any other taxpayer whose Federal income tax return reflects tax consequences or a tax strategy arising from such a transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the class of persons required to disclose under the listed-transaction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — qualified organization not treated as a participant (paragraph (e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified organization to which the conservation easement is donated is not treated as a participant under §1.6011-4(c)(3)(i)(A) in a syndicated conservation easement transaction described in paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of section 4965 — carveout for donee organizations (paragraph (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified organization to which the real property interest is donated is not treated under section 4965 of the Code as a party to the transaction described in paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rescues certain donee organizations from being treated as implicated under section 4965 in these transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure equivalence for prior Notice 2017-10 filings (paragraph (g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A taxpayer who disclosed their participation in a transaction pursuant to Notice 2017-10 and in accordance with §1.6011-4 before October 8, 2024, is treated as having made the disclosure required under this section and §1.6011-4 for the years covered by that prior disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids duplicative reporting for years already covered by Notice 2017-10 disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability dates (paragraph (h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of transactions as listed transactions is effective October 8, 2024. Applicability date for material advisors: notwithstanding §301.6111-3(b)(4)(i) and (iii), material advisors are required to disclose only if they have made a tax statement on or after October 8, 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules therefore reach some prior transactions (subject to statute of limitations rules) but limit material-advisor disclosure obligations to statements made on/after Oct 8, 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material advisor — definition, triggering events, and no timing exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A material advisor is defined in §301.6111-3(b) as a person who makes a 'tax statement' and derives gross income in excess of the threshold amount. A person becomes a material advisor when: (1) the person provides material aid, assistance, or advice as described; (2) the person directly or indirectly derives gross income in excess of the threshold amount (generally $10,000 for listed transactions); and (3) the transaction is entered into by the taxpayer to whom (or for whose benefit) the person provided the tax statement (or when a tax statement is provided to another material advisor, when the taxpayer to whom that advisor provided a tax statement enters into the transaction). There is no exception for appraisers engaged after an easement is put in place; they can be material advisors based on statements or actions after an easement is in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a transaction later becomes a listed transaction, a person who previously provided a tax statement can be treated as becoming a material advisor on the date the transaction is identified as a listed transaction, but resulting obligations are limited to actions required thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory coverage despite SECURE 2.0 Act (scope and three covered classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations continue to identify and cover three major classes of abusive syndicated conservation easement transactions: (1) transactions involving contributions occurring before December 30, 2022; (2) transactions for which a charitable contribution deduction is not automatically disallowed by section 170(h)(7) (including those that satisfy statutory exceptions) but that nevertheless meet the listed-transaction elements; and (3) transactions that substitute the contribution of a fee simple interest in real property for the contribution of a conservation easement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations explicitly do not adopt an exception for the three statutory exceptions in section 170(h)(7)(C)–(E); transactions meeting the listed-transaction elements will still be listed even if not automatically disallowed by section 170(h)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with reporting and statute-of-limitations rules (§1.6011-4 and §301.6501(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations identify a listed transaction but do not amend the general reporting rules in §1.6011-4; §1.6011-4(e)(2)(i) requires reporting of transactions entered into prior to publication of guidance identifying a transaction as a listed transaction if the statute of limitations for assessment of tax is still open when the transaction becomes a listed transaction. If a taxpayer required to disclose fails to do so, section 6501(c)(10) provides that the time for assessment does not expire before one year after the earlier of (1) the date the taxpayer provides the required information or (2) the date a material advisor meets section 6112 requirements in response to a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on 'open year' determination and penalty abatement rules are outside the scope of these final regulations but other cited regulations (and statutes) control these procedural consequences.
